story: Arizona appeals court tosses sentence over AI video of slain victim (ABC News, 13 Oct 2026)

item.title: Manslaughter sentence tossed over AI-generated video of slain victim used at trial
item.curator_note: Arizona appeals court threw out a manslaughter sentence because the judge was shown an AI-generated video of the victim speaking; first appeals ruling on AI victim statements.

entry.headline: An Arizona appeals court threw out a killer's prison sentence because the judge had watched an AI video of the victim speaking.
entry.summary: ABC News reports that the Arizona Court of Appeals, in a 30 Sep 2026 ruling, upheld Gabriel Paul Horcasitas' manslaughter conviction for the 2021 road rage killing of Christopher Pelkey but ordered a new sentencing, because the trial judge had been shown an AI-generated video in which Pelkey's likeness and voice, scripted by his sister, spoke of forgiveness. The three judges found that weighing the video made the hearing "fundamentally unfair", saying it blurred the line between what the family believed Pelkey would say and his own voice; his sister told ABC News the family has no regrets and she will read the script herself at the new hearing.
entry.importance_line: Families of crime victims may lose the option of speaking through an AI recreation of their loved one at sentencing, and courts gain a warning that such videos can make a sentence unfair, though this is one state appeals panel and the resentencing has no date yet.
